agent.result_text:
Held people and held claims now count in every total again. A hold now only affects the pools: the held person gets no cut, and their share is spread over the others. `bin/e2e` passed all 4 acceptance tests.

The server and the screen each had their own copy of the rule, so I changed both:

- **Server** (`person/Person.java`): the rule for whether a claim counts no longer checks the claim's own hold or the person's hold dates. That rule feeds the rollup lines, closing a period and statements. Pools (`pool/Pools.java`) has its own hold check and is unchanged.
- **Screen**:
  - `people/usePeople.ts`: `heldOn` now looks only at retirement, not at hold dates.
  - `claims/useClaims.ts` and `periods/usePeriods.ts`: these no longer drop claims marked held.
  - Every total on the screen (claimed, due-totals, overdue, aging, months, tags, export, summary, period figures) goes through these helpers, so they all count held claims again.
  - Backing never looked at holds, so I left it as it was.

A retired person's open and pending claims still drop out of the totals once the sheet's today reaches their retirement date, unless a statement binds them. Only the hold part was removed.

Nothing changes in the stored data: the hold flag and hold dates are still saved and shown ("held yes/no", the hold dates list), and the hold audit records are unchanged. I also updated the code comments that described the old behaviour. The last two of those (in `usePeriods.ts` and `aging.slot.tsx`) were made after that test run started, but they are comment-only.

probe.probe_text:
I changed nothing. I read the claim, figure, permission and holiday code myself; two read-only helpers surveyed periods/imports and holds/statements/pools, and I checked their key points against the code. Java paths are under `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/`; front-end paths are under `src/main/frontend/features/`.

# 1. Figures and the rules behind them

## Per claim (the claim row)

**`claim-due`**: the screen works this out itself with `claimDueCents` (`claims/useClaims.ts`). The server has its own copy in `Figures.due` (`claim/Figures.java:58`).
- If the claim has a **fixed due** (`due`, set when it was settled), it shows that.
- Else, if a statement **binds** it (`stated`), it shows the bound figure (`statedDue`). That figure already includes the floor and late charge it had then, so its late charge no longer follows today.
- Else it is **live**: amount × the grade's rate ÷ 100, rounded to 2 decimals (`Figures.live` / `dueCents`).
  - Rate: from `Rates.pct` / `claimRateOn`, for the person's grade in force on the claim's date (`gradeOn(claim.date)`).
  - A rate saved with a from-date on or after the sheet's today (**forward-only**, `forwardAfter`) is skipped for claims added before it was saved (decided by `seq`).
  - If the sheet itself has no rate, the parent sheets' rates apply (up to 3 levels up), then the sheet it was cloned from.
  - No rate at all shows **n/a**.
- The live figure is then raised to at least the **floor** in force on the claim's date (`Settings.floor`, default 1.00).
- Then the **late charge** is added (`Figures.charge` / `lateChargeCents`).
  - It applies only to an OPEN or PENDING claim that is not deferred, not a correction and not `waived`.
  - For every full 30 days past `overdueFrom` (due-by plus the grade's grace days), it adds the late percent in force on that 30-day boundary date. Each step is charged on the figure plus the charges before it (compounding) and rounded separately. A 0.00 percent adds nothing.
- A **correction** (`isCorrection`: a negative amount) gets no floor and no late charge.

**Rounding** (`Figures.rounding`, sent as `halfUp`):
- If a dated `rounding` setting is in force on the claim's date, it decides.
- Otherwise: half up if the claim is dated before the **policy date** (`policyDate`, which defaults to the sheet's today), half to even on or after it.
- A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects.

**`claim-due-by`** (`DueBy.of`, `BuildClaim`):
- It is fixed when the claim is added: the terms-th **business day** after the claim date, skipping Saturdays, Sundays and the sheet's holidays.
- The terms are looked up on the day the claim is created, not on its date: the person's own terms (`termsOn`), else their grade's, else the sheet's (default 14).
- The number of terms used is stored as `dueTerms`.
- Re-dating the claim or changing the terms later does not move the due-by.
- Adding a holiday re-fixes the due-by (`RefixDueBys`) for every claim that is not SETTLED or VOID and is due on or after that holiday. It is recalculated from the claim's current date with the stored `dueTerms`.

**The due-by also decides:**
- the claim's **period** (`claim-period`, `periodOf(periods, c.dueBy)`);
- whether a closed period freezes the claim;
- the claim's number;
- whether it is a late entry;
- the period cap.

**`claim-overdue`** (`overdue`): OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `dueBy + grace` is before the sheet's today.

**`claim-number`** (`ClaimNumbers.next`): given when the claim is opened (or, for a REVIEW claim, when it is reviewed).
- While `periodNumberingFrom` is set and today is on or after it, the number is `<period>-n`, or `X-n` if the due-by is in no period.
- Otherwise it is `FY<yyyy>-n`, counted by the due-by's fiscal year (using `fiscalStartMonth`) and shared across the sheet tree.
- Voided claims keep their number and numbers are never reused. Reassigning or splitting a claim gives it a new number.

**Status** (`ClaimStatus`, `ClaimAction`, `ApplyClaimStatus`):
- DRAFT→OPEN→SETTLED.
- A clerk settling over the **clerk limit** (`clerkLimit`: the grade's own limit on today, else the sheet's) sends it to PENDING instead. A steward or the person's `approver` then approves it (SETTLED) or rejects it (back to OPEN).
- If the due is over the **review threshold** when opened, the claim goes to REVIEW with no number until a steward reviews it.
- DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, REVIEW and SETTLED can go to VOID. A SETTLED claim can be voided only by a steward, within 7 days (`SETTLED_VOID_DAYS`).
- A DRAFT can be DELETED, and restored only on the same sheet-today.

**Settling** freezes the claim's due at its figure then (the bound figure or the live one, plus floor and late charge).
- "Settle as of" a date uses the due as it stood at the end of that date (`ValidateClaimStatus`).
- **Resettle** (steward only) fixes the due again at today's unbound live figure.
- **Settle part** splits an amount off and settles the new claim, judging the rules on the original claim.

**Refusals when changing status:**
- Four-eyes rule: the opener or the last editor (`editedBy`) cannot settle or approve.
- Proof rule: if the due is over the **proof threshold** (the grade's, else the sheet's, on the claim's date), the claim needs at least one proof, and one of each of the sheet's `proofKinds`.
- **Note threshold**: an over-threshold claim needs a note to be opened.
- A **deferred** claim cannot be settled.
- **Period cap** (`atCap`): opening is refused if the person already has that many OPEN or PENDING claims due in the capped period.
- A **flagged** person's claims can be opened only by a steward.
- If the sheet has **void reasons**, a void must give one of them.

**Other claim flags:**
- `deferred`: only an OPEN claim can be deferred, and only to a date after today. While deferred it is out of every total, never overdue, has no charge and is not bound by statements.
- `waived`: steward only, OPEN or PENDING claims. The claim gets no charge from then on.
- `held`: OPEN or PENDING claims only. It is display-only and still counts.
- `lateEntry`: set when a soft-closed period contains the due-by when the claim is added.
- `remindedOn` / escalated: one reminder per sheet-today. If the gap since the last reminder is at least `escalateAfter` days, the claim is escalated once.
- `claim-review-late`: a REVIEW claim is late when the day it entered REVIEW plus `reviewSla` days is before today. The screen gets that day by parsing the log text.
- `batch`: the number of the bulk settle that settled it.
- `splitFrom`, `ref` (unique on the sheet, case-insensitive), `tags`, `proofs` (split into receipts and photos), `lockedBy`.

**Edits:**
- Only a DRAFT can be edited. It must not be locked by another user's open editor.
- If the claim has lines, its amount is their sum.
- It cannot be dated after its person's retirement date, or inside a past retirement.
- A correction must name a SETTLED claim of the same person, and cannot exceed what remains of it (`Claims.remaining`).

## Per person (`person-*`; worked out on the screen in `claims/claims.slot.tsx:141-165`, and again on the server in `Rollup.snapshot`)

**Which claims count** (`Person.counts`, `live()` on the screen):
- OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED claims count; deferred ones do not.
- Once `retiredOut` applies (today has reached the retirement date), OPEN and PENDING claims drop out unless a statement binds them. SETTLED claims still count.
- **Holds take nothing out of the totals** in the current code.

**`person-claimed`** (`countsClaimed` / `claimedLive` + `claimed`): the amounts of the counted claims added up, leaving out corrections.

**`person-due-total`** (`personDueCents`): the counted claims' dues added up, at most the **cap** in force on today.
- It is n/a only if there is no rate today and no claim has a figure.
- **`person-excess`** is the amount above the cap.
- **`person-settled-total`** and **`person-open-total`** are the uncapped sums of the SETTLED part and the OPEN-or-PENDING part.

**`person-overdue-count` / `-total`** (`overdueFigures`): how many counted claims are overdue, and their dues added up.

**Sheet totals** (`useSheetTotals`):
- Claimed is a plain sum.
- Due and overdue are **trimmed**: the single highest and lowest person are left out when there are 3 or more.
- `Rollup` writes ROLLUP and TOTALS audit lines, plus an ALERT line when a person's due crosses above `alertThreshold`.

**Statements** (`TakeStatement`):
- Any non-viewer can take one.
- Each counted claim is bound to its current due (`stated`, `statedDue`); all other claims of the person are unbound.
- `statedTotal` is their sum, capped; `statementDate` is today (or the as-of date).
- **Cancel** is steward only. It unbinds every claim of the person and does not restore earlier bindings.
- Reassigning or splitting a claim also unbinds it.

**Other person figures:**
- `grade` is the one in force on today (dated `grades`).
- `terms`: the person's own terms (dated).
- `flag` is shown while today is on or before its until-date. Its only effect is the steward-only open rule.
- Retirement: `retired` is true as soon as any date is set. It refuses claims dated after the retirement date or inside a past retirement.
- `snapshots`: due-total lines recorded each time today moves.
- `statementLines`.
- `clashing`: the name or an alias is used on another sheet in the tree. Edits are refused until the person is renamed.

**Holds and pools:**
- A person's **hold** only gives them a 0.00 cut in pools (`Pools.cuts`). So does any retirement date, even a future one.
- Pool cuts: pot × share ÷ eligible shares, rounded half to even. The remainder goes to the smallest non-zero cut.
- A cut is only worked out when the pool is balanced (shares total 100.00).

## Periods (`PeriodCloser`, `ClosedPeriods`, `periods/usePeriods.ts`)

**Which period a claim is in** is decided by its **due-by**, not its claim date.

**Close** (default: clerk or steward, by the permission matrix):
- Freezes per-person totals as of the end of the period's last day.
- Uses each claim's status at that point, taken from the claim log.
- Also freezes the **carried** figure: OPEN or PENDING claims from earlier periods, plus imported openings.
- While a period is fully closed, every change to a claim due in it is refused (`PeriodClosedException`), including add, edit, status changes, split, defer, lock, proof, resettle, reassign and redate.

**Soft close**: freezes the figures the same way, but claims can still be changed. New claims due in it are marked `lateEntry`.

**Reopen**: steward by default. It clears the frozen figures. A **locked** period cannot be reopened.

**Lock / unlock**: steward only. Locking only blocks a reopen.

**Auto-close**: when today moves past a period's end date plus `graceDays`, the period is closed. This happens without a permission check and skips soft-closed periods.

**While a period is open**, only the screen works out its figures.

## Imports and paste

**Import openings**:
- Each line is `name,period,amount`; all lines are checked first, and one bad line refuses the whole import.
- Each amount is added to any opening already there; it does not replace it.
- It only changes a closed period's carried figure if the period is reopened and closed again.
- There is no role check and no period-state check.

**Import people**:
- A line matching an existing name or alias edits that person; the grade is set from today.
- Otherwise it adds a person. A blank grade becomes `defaultGrade`.

**Paste claims**:
- It is all or nothing. A line with the same date and note as an unused DRAFT of that person updates that DRAFT.
- Every line is then opened, under the same rules as a single open.
- The count it returns includes the updated DRAFTs.

## Who may do what

**Roles**: clerk (the default), steward, viewer.
- A delegation makes a user a steward while today is within its dates.
- A viewer may do nothing, and nobody may change an archived sheet.

**Permission matrix** (`Settings.allows`):
- By default, open, settle, void and close are allowed to clerks and stewards; reassign and reopen to stewards only.
- The defaults can be changed per sheet.

**Steward only**:
- re-date, waive, resettle, review, void a settled claim
- lock or unlock a period
- flag, merge, transfer, undo transfer
- cancel a statement
- archive, clone

**Today**: the sheet's own date, not the clock.
- Changing it releases every claim lock, writes snapshots, auto-closes periods and writes rollups.
- The **as-of** view rebuilds the sheet as it stood at the end of a past date. The screen is read-only while it is set.

## Where the code contradicts itself
- **Holds.** About ten doc comments still say a hold, or a claim dated within one, takes claims out of the totals. These include `ClaimStatus.isOpen`, `useClaims.isOpen`, `Claim.held` in `useClaims.ts`, `usePeople.ts`, two adjacent comments in `claims.slot.tsx:147-150`, `PeriodCloser`, `TakeStatement`, and the `hold.POST.yml` files. The code (`Person.counts`, `heldOn` → `retiredOut`) takes nothing out.
- **"Dated in" vs "due by".** Many comments say claims "dated in" a period; the code uses the due-by. `Claim.getDueBy`'s comment says the due-by is the date plus calendar terms of the grade on that date. The code uses business days, with terms looked up on the day the claim is created.
- **PENDING claims and statements.** `claims.slot.tsx:99` says a PENDING claim shows its live figure. The code shows the bound figure.
- **Period figures.** The screen's period "Due" column is its own sum. It never shows the server's frozen `closedTotal`.
- **Roles.** Setting a role has no permission check, so any clerk can make themselves a steward.

# 2. How hard it was to follow

It was hard. There is no single place a new developer could read. The money rules are written twice, in Java (`Figures`, `Person.counts`, `Rollup`, `PeriodCloser`) and in TypeScript (`useClaims.ts`, `useRates.ts`, `usePeriods.ts`, `useSheetTotals.ts`), and the screen shows the TypeScript results. The other rules are spread over about 150 one-method pipeline classes and their YAML wiring, and the long doc comments often contradict each other and the code (holds most of all), so you can't trust them without reading the code underneath.
